blocks.text: This article describes adding a custom root certificate for a third-party proxy-chaining service or isolation profile in the Zscaler Admin Console. The Root Certificates page already carries the default Zscaler Root Certificate, which cannot be edited. You can add up to 10 root certificates for your organization. To learn about downloading certificates for SSL/TLS Inspection, see Choosing the CA Certificate for SSL/TLS Inspection.

blocks.item: If your upstream proxy (third-party proxy service) is performing SSL/TLS Inspection, Zscaler requires you to install the root certificates of the proxy service to sign the MITM certificates.
To add a root certificate for proxy chaining:
From the navigation menu, go to Internet Access > Resources > Root Certificates.
The Add Root Certificates drawer appears.
In the Add Root Certificates drawer:
Name: Enter a name for your certificate.
Type: Select Proxy Chaining from the drop-down menu.
File (.pem): Drag & drop the file, or browse and select the required root certificate (PEM file) from your system.
